title: Introducing The Campaign Agent That Turns Goals Into Growth
summary: Most campaigns run blind to every other campaign hitting the same customer. Campaign Agent arbitrates across all of them, in real time, in the customer's favor.
body_markdown:
For years, marketing has run on the belief that we could predict customers well enough to build their path in advance: segmenting, scoring, and slotting them into a pre-built journey.


That doesn’t hold up anymore. Customers wander, double back, and change their mind. Tools marketers use today still run on rigid, rules-based logic: predefined segments, fixed journeys, static messages. It’s brittle, expensive to maintain, and blind to what any other campaign is doing to the same customer at the same time.


To grow in this era, you need to meet every customer with an experience shaped by their intent, not a segment. But no marketing team can hand-build that for every single customer, and full one-to-one personalization isn’t cost-effective at scale either. Most marketers don’t need or want infinite unique messaging.


What if your team had an agent that could take a business goal and turn it into a live, adaptive campaign that reads customer intent and delivers the right experience across every channel, without you having to script every path?


## Meet your campaign agent


You set the strategy, ground output in your brand, define guardrails and approve adjustments along the way. That’s the work marketers are best at. Campaign Agent turns that direction into a live campaign that keeps adapting.


What Campaign Agent does:


- **Campaign Assembly** : Campaign Agent assembles the audience, content, and channels to hit goals.
- **Content Personalization** : generates brand-compliant, multichannel, multilingual content variations at scale, grounded in your CMS assets and brand guidelines, with marketers reviewing and approving along the way.
- **Send Prioritization** : evaluates each customer’s intent and context in real time to decide which campaign should reach them, prioritizing or suppressing sends so no one gets competing, redundant messages.


That last part is the real shift. Today, every campaign runs in its own lane, blind to what every other campaign is doing to the same customer at the same time. Campaign Agent runs an agentic learning loop grounded in your own data, combining machine learning to spot patterns across customers with LLM reasoning to interpret what they actually need. It isn’t managing one campaign in isolation; it’s arbitrating across all of them in favor of what’s right for the customer at that moment.


## How Campaign Agent works, step by step


Campaign Agent’s workflow runs in two phases: marketers set direction, then the agent takes that direction live.


### Phase 1: Coworking


- **Campaign** : A marketer prompts Campaign Agent with their campaign goals (e.g., “Build a campaign to grow subscriptions”). The agent then turns that into a full campaign, all aligned to a brief with a goal and KPI target, live dates, channels, budget, audience size with inclusion/exclusion criteria, and a first pass at content variants.
- **Content** : Grounded in that campaign output, Campaign Agent then generates the actual promotional assets. They’re multichannel (email, RCS, MMS, SMS) and multilingual (English, French, Spanish), personalized to your data sources and checked against approved brand guidelines.


Marketers stay in control at every step here, iterating and approving before anything goes live.


###
Phase 2: Decisioning


Once a campaign is live, Campaign Agent continuously marries your strategy (goal, budget, brief) with each customer’s real-time intent (browsing history, propensity models, past purchases) across three moves:


- **Prioritization** : Decides which campaign actually reaches a given customer, suppressing the ones that don’t fit. For example, holding back a seasonal campaign and a welcome journey in favor of a more relevant promo campaign.
- **Assembly** : Picks the exact language, content variant, channel, and send time for each individual customer (e.g., English, Variant 3, delivered by SMS in the morning).
- **Optimization** : Keeps adjusting the live campaign based on performance: increasing budget, rebalancing channel weight, pausing an underperforming offer, shifting send time, or expanding audience with lookalikes.


This is the loop that makes Campaign Agent different from a one-and-done campaign build. It’s not just assembling a campaign once, it’s actively arbitrating and tuning it for every customer, re-looping and nudging the marketer to optimize every day it’s live.


## Start using Campaign Agent


Campaign Agent is[Generally Available](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_mktg_agentforce.htm&release=264&type=5) in Marketing Cloud Next this October. Resources and examples will be continually shared to help you get the most out of Campaign Agent.


This changes what marketing teams are actually responsible for. You’re no longer building and babysitting individual journeys. You’re setting goals and grounding in your brand, and letting an agent handle the moment-to-moment work of matching each customer to the right experience. That’s a fundamentally different job, and it’s the one marketing teams have wanted for years but never had the tooling to do. Set the goal and watch Campaign Agent run with it.
